recent_findings.summary: `.github/workflows/pr-merge-gate.yml` checks out the PR head SHA and runs `python3 tools/loom_flow.py ...` from that checkout; this preserves head binding but executes PR-supplied code as part of a required check, which is a host-trust boundary decision for repos accepting untrusted external PRs.

disposition.summary: Document and enforce contributor-trust assumptions before making `loom-pr-merge-gate` required, or redesign the workflow to avoid executing arbitrary PR-head code (e.g., pinned tooling or API-fetched artifacts) for untrusted contribution models.

recent_findings.summary: `controlled-merge` treats any branch rules/ruleset read error as `missing_inputs`, which can block merges even when branch protection is readable and sufficient to prove required contexts; this appears stricter than the documented contract that only requires at least one readable enforcement source (branch protection or active ruleset).

disposition.summary: Align code and contract: either (a) only fail closed on ruleset read errors when branch protection is also unavailable (or when ruleset enforcement is required by policy), or (b) update the contract to explicitly require successful ruleset readback even when branch protection is present.
